html:
The Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in, "people of the river", are a First Nation of the Yukon River around Dawson City, in Canada's Yukon. Most descend from the Hän-speaking people, an Athabaskan group who have lived along the Yukon River for thousands of years.

They travelled widely through their land, catching salmon in the Yukon River and hunting caribou from the Fortymile and Porcupine herds, along with moose, small game, plants and berries. Their main fishing camp stood where the Klondike River meets the Yukon.

In 1896 gold was found on a creek nearby, and the Klondike Gold Rush brought tens of thousands of people. Dawson City was built on and around the fishing camp. Chief Isaac moved his people downriver to Moosehide. The Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in signed a land claim with Canada in 1998. Their neighbours include the Vuntut Gwitchin and the Na-Cho Nyäk Dun.
